channel.title: Sleepwing dev notes
channel.description: Build-in-public notes from Sleepwing — the privacy-first macOS desktop pet that watches your AI coding agents.

item.title: Landing in the pane, not just the app
item.description: An agent inside tmux sees the pane's pty, which no terminal owns as a tab, so tab-exact return silently degraded to activating the app for every multiplexer user. 0.6.6-beta.1 build 23 selects the agent's pane, then focuses its attached client's tab. Panes are addressed by tmux's own %pane/$session ids, because a colon in a session name breaks name-based targeting outright.

item.title: A nudge is a moment, not a state
item.description: A health nudge outranks "working" by design, but an unanswered one had no expiry and masked five running agent sessions. It now lapses after ten minutes — the same window a snooze earns — and closes its record as skipped. Shipped in 0.6.5-beta.1 build 22. Plus a signing preflight that blamed the wrong side.

item.title: When the signal stops, say so
item.description: If a working session sends no lifecycle event for 30 minutes, Sleepwing marks it "status unconfirmed" instead of faking a green state — health timing pauses, the next real event resumes it. Plus the ops version of the same lesson: our metrics cron was silently down 17 days.

item.title: Landing on the exact terminal tab
item.description: Builds 18 and 19 shipped so a task click lands on the exact terminal tab hosting the session, via the controlling-TTY device name — including the macOS ttyname()/e_tdev detour that forced the second build. Plus hook-loss warnings and full-screen yield.

item.title: Sleepwing 0.6.0 beta ships notarized; celebration timing fixed; five guide pages live
item.description: The first notarized public beta (0.6.0 build 17) is on GitHub Releases; the celebration animation now rests its weight on on-model frames; and the site grew honest comparison and notification guides for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and TRAE.
